The Afternoon Before (Grounding) * **The "No New Things" Rule:** Don’t try to rewrite your jokes, practice a new song, or change your poem today. Your material is what it is. Trust the work you’ve already put in. * **Hydrate and Eat Lightly:** A nervous stomach does not play well with a heavy meal. Eat something light and clean about 2–3 hours before the show. Drink plenty of water (but stop chugging it an hour before so you don't have to pee when your name is called). * **Burn Off Excess Cortisol:** If you feel like you are vibrating with anxiety, go for a quick 15-minute walk or do some light stretching. Physical movement helps release the buildup of stress hormones. ### 2. Arriving at the Venue (Scouting) * **Arrive Early:** Nothing ruins your energy faster than rushing. Arrive with plenty of time to sign up, find a seat, and get a lay of the land. * **De-mystify the Room:** Walk up to the stage before the show starts if you can. Look at where the mic is. Look at the crowd from that perspective. Once your brain "sees" the space, it stops imagining a worst-case scenario. * **Limit Your Alcohol:** It is incredibly tempting to have three beers to "take the edge off." Don't do it. Alcohol dulls your reaction time, slurs your speech, and actually *increases* anxiety as it wears off. Stick to one drink maximum, or stick to water/soda. ### 3. In the "Green Room" / Waiting to Go On (Focusing) * **Accept the Butterflies:** When your heart starts racing, don't panic. Tell yourself: *“This is just adrenaline. My body is getting ready to do something exciting.”* Reframe "nervousness" as "excitement." They feel identical physically. * **The 4-7-8 Breathing Technique:** If you feel your chest tightening, do this: Breathe in through your nose for 4 seconds, hold your breath for 7 seconds, and exhale slowly through your mouth for 8 seconds. Do this 4 times. It physically forces your nervous system to exit "fight or flight" mode.
